records.issue_text: [BUG] Wrapping the entire event listener in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) changes cleanup semantics: previously the role/client/group removal cleanup ran unconditionally, now it is skipped entirely when the feature is disabled. A realm that had fine-grained admin permissions, then has the feature disabled (a supported profile change), accumulates stale authorization resources/policies on every subsequent role, client, and group deletion; when the feature is re-enabled those stale grants evaluate against deleted entities. The old code deliberately cleaned up in the disabled state; the new guard removes that safety net.
records.rationale: The diff in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` wraps all cleanup handling for `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent`, and `GroupRemovedEvent` inside `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`. Previously, these events *always* executed cleanup via `management(...).roles()/clients()/groups().setPermissionsEnabled(..., false);`. With the new guard, when the feature is disabled those cleanup calls are skipped entirely, leaving any existing fine-grained authz artifacts unmodified on deletions. records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] canExchangeTo(ClientModel, ClientModel, AccessToken) throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning false, so the V2 evaluator cannot express a deny for token-exchange. Any token-exchange path that consults the client permission evaluator while V2 fine-grained authz is enabled gets a 500 instead of a clean 403/deny, an availability defect on an authn/authz-critical flow and a silent behavioral change for existing deployments relying on per-client token-exchange permissions.

records.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel) throws UnsupportedOperationException even though it is a read API inherited from the shipped ClientPermissions contract, so any existing caller in the codebase or out-of-tree extension gets a runtime crash instead of a boolean during the V1→V2 transition. This is a silent public-surface/contract break on the shared base class: existing code that queries isPermissionsEnabled (admin console client representations expose permissionsEnabled) will throw UnsupportedOperationException with a 500 rather than a graceful value, so enabling the V2 path breaks readers of per-client permission state with no expand/contract phase where the old implementation remains callable.
records.rationale: ClientPermissionsV2 explicitly overrides the inherited read API `isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel)` and implements it as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (same for several other previously-available methods). Since MgmtPermissionsV2 now returns `new ClientPermissionsV2(...)` from `clients()`, any code path using `management(...).clients().isPermissionsEnabled(client)` will now deterministically crash at runtime instead of returning a boolean, which is a behavioral break introduced by this diff.
